results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Retaining critical talent and institutional knowledge
results.content: An organisation’s most valuable knowledge is often held by the people who understand its customers, systems, processes, relationships and operating environment. When experienced employees leave without proper knowledge transfer, the organization can lose capabilities that took years to develop. Talent retention is therefore a strategic leadership priority. CEOs must understand why critical employees stay, what may cause them to leave and whether the organization provides the environment, opportunities and recognition needed to retain them.

results.title: Prudential Bank urges Ghanaian SMEs to improve readiness for Chinese market
results.content: Prudential Bank Limited has urged Ghanaian businesses seeking to enter the Chinese market to strengthen their market research, business planning and trade relationships to improve their prospects of securing export financing. The Bank’s Acting Managing Director, Ebow Quayson, made the call during a panel discussion at the Ghana–China Zero Tariff Forum 2026, where he discussed the financing challenges facing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with exportable products but limited export records, conventional collateral or confirmed purchase orders.

results.title: NPP Germany mobilisation dinner focuses on unity and 2028 election strategy
results.content: DÜSSELDORF, Germany – The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Germany Branch has brought together national party leaders, Members of Parliament and supporters for a mobilisation dinner to discuss the party's rebuilding efforts and preparations for Ghana's 2028 general elections. The event, held on Saturday, November 21, 2026, under the theme “The Road to 2028: A Night of Vision and Political Renewal”, provided an opportunity to examine the party's defeat in the 2024 elections, its political and economic message, and the role of its diaspora branches in the next election campaign.

results.title: Do not ban — expand your facilities (Wisdom From The Akwapim Mountains — Episode 12 revisited)
results.content: In the early days, admission to Class One was not by intelligence, but by a physical test. A child stretched his hand over his head to touch the opposite ear. If the hand could not reach, he was sent home. My late father-in-law suffered this. He was a very bright boy, but very short. He waited until age nine to enter Class One — not because his mind was not ready, but because his body was short. We laugh at that system today. Yet we are repeating it in a new form. Then we measured the body. Now we measure years spent in class. In both cases, we fail to measure the mind.

results.title: DDEP bondholders have already sacrificed enough – Amin Adam kicks against early buyback offer
results.content: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam says DDEP bondholders have already sacrificed enough towards addressing Ghana's economic challenges and must not be pushed into another deal that leaves them worse off. In a Facebook post on the government's voluntary bond buyback, Dr Amin Adam said bondholders accepted painful cuts under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) to help the country recover and must be allowed to fully benefit from their long wait, which is nearing its end. "Bondholders have already paid their share. Under the DDEP, they accepted lower interest and waited longer to get their money back. They helped carry the cost of fixing the economy, and the government now celebrates the fall in the national debt to GDP ratio," he said.

results.title: Amin Adam questions Ato Forson over transparency of bond buyback offer
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson is facing questions over the government's voluntary Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) bond buyback, with his predecessor, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, urging him to uphold the standards he championed while in opposition. In a Facebook post reacting to the government's offer to buy back DDEP bonds ahead of their full repayment in February 2027, Dr Amin Adam questioned the rationale behind the move, arguing that it could disadvantage bondholders.
